item.title: Max Verstappen defends British teammate after social media abuse: ‘I need to speak out’
item.description: Max Verstappen has hit out at “personal attacks” directed at teammate Chris Lulham on social media while competing at an endurance event in Portugal over the weekend. The four-time F1 world champion was racing in the GT World Challenge on Saturday for his own independent team, Verstappen Racing, and was joined by British drivers Lulham and Ben Barnicoat. In the middle phase of the endurance race on Saturday, Lulham received a drive-through penalty which pushed his team down to 24th when the Dutchman took over. Verstappen recovered to finish ninth, in a finale which included a dramatic late overtake on Charles Leclerc’s brother, Arthur. VERSTAPPEN VS LECLERC 🔥 Max Verstappen did battle with Arthur Leclerc during an incredible recovery drive in the GT World Challenge that saw the Dutchman finish P9 following a drive-through penalty. pic.twitter.com/9ZZhkQyUxS — Sky Sports F1 (@SkySportsF1) October 18, 2026 Yet in the aftermath, Lulham was subject to abuse online and Verstappen – just a few days after Franco Colapinto implored his fans to stop abusing fellow F1 drivers – released a short statement on Instagram condemning those responsible. "I also feel I need to speak up about the hate and harassment Chris has received after the race,” he said. “Everyone can have their opinions about what happened on track, but these personal attacks are not okay. "Chris had a really strong stint, and mistakes can happen. There’s no place for this kind of abuse in our sport or anywhere else." Verstappen’s message comes a few days after Alpine F1 driver Colapinto told his fanbase “you’re not helping me” after a number of incidents involving social media abuse of fellow drivers on the grid. Verstappen was racing in between two F1 triple-headers, the second of which starts with the United States Grand Prix in Austin this weekend. The Red Bull driver has won the last two races, in Malaysia and Singapore, and is currently fourth in the drivers’ standings.

item.title: Are the Knicks ready for what's next? New York's repeat bid begins with nowhere to hide in wide-open NBA
item.description: NEW YORK — Everywhere you looked, it seemed, there they were. Fresh off the run of a lifetime — a 16-3 sprint through the postseason, headlined by some of the most remarkable blowouts and comebacks in NBA playoff history, capped off by an all-time individual performance in the NBA Finals to clinch the franchise's first NBA championship in 53 years — the New York Knicks spent their summers basking in the afterglow, enjoying the fruits of their labors. A ticker-tape parade through the Canyon of Heroes in lower Manhattan. Guest spots on "The Tonight Show," "Late Night," "The View," and "Good Morning America." Ceremonial first pitches at Yankee Stadium and Citi Field , and streets renamed in their honor. Places of prominence in the stands at the World Cup and U.S. Open . Featured appearances at both "Saturday Night's Main Event" and "Saturday Night Live." Jalen Brunson heard MVP chants at City Hall . Karl-Anthony Towns heard "Knicks in five!" during a honeymoon trip to the Serengeti. Mike Brown heard a standing ovation when he and his wife walked into the Polo Bar. Join or create a Yahoo Fantasy Basketball league for the 2026-27 NBA season Everywhere the head coach turned, another well-wisher. More congratulations. Another hand to shake. "I had nowhere to hide," Brown said at the Knicks' media day session last month. And now, neither does his team. On Tuesday night, the Knicks will experience one final celebration of what they accomplished in June. They'll watch a banner raised to the rafters of Madison Square Garden. They'll receive championship rings laden with enough ice to turn autumn into winter. They'll revel in it all one more time, feeling the adulation of the New York faithful wash over them … … and then look down from the rafters and see Joel Embiid, LeBron James, Tyrese Maxey, Jaylen Brown, VJ Edgecombe and the rest of the Philadelphia 76ers, all champing at the bit for the opportunity to knock the newly anointed kings right off the top of the mountain. "I mean, obviously, you look at it on paper, and that's a hell of a group," Knicks guard Landry Shamet said at Monday's practice ahead of Tuesday's season opener. "We know that, and I think that's why a lot of our focus has got to be on that, and the ring and the celebration has kind of gotta be secondary. Because our job is our job, and it is 0-0, and I don't think any of us are satisfied with going home with just this championship. We've got things we're still striving toward." You've surely heard it by now. No NBA champion has repeated since the 2017 and 2018 Golden State Warriors. The last Eastern Conference champion to return to the Finals the following year? The LeBron-led Cleveland Cavaliers that did battle with those Dubs. Such is life in Adam Silver's Parity of Opportunity Era, a moment in NBA history in which it seems champions are built to be broken. After the parades and the TV appearances and the ovations and the banners and the rings, there's one more reward awaiting a champion: the proverbial bullseye on your back. You survived the 100-game marathon to reach the top of the mountain and hoist the trophy? Congratulations. All your hard work has earned you is … more hard work. Harder work. Every opponent's best shot, every single night. "To repeat is gonna take an even higher sense of discipline and execution, and we're gonna have to even be better than what we showed in the playoffs," Towns said. "So, all of us are aware that we're gonna have to bring a whole other level to the table if we expect to have a chance to repeat." After taking on the new-look Sixers on ring night, the Knicks head to Boston to play a Celtics team featuring a healthy Jayson Tatum, new arrival Paul George and old pal Mitchell Robinson. Then, it's back to Manhattan for a visit from the Orlando Magic, led by new head coach Sean Sweeney, who just four months ago was devising schemes to try to stifle New York as the defensive coordinator in San Antonio. Two nights later, the Pistons come to MSG, eager to pick up where they left off last season, when they won all three of their regular-season meetings with the Knicks — by a total of 84 points . In early November, they'll have a pair of meetings with the Cleveland Cavaliers, whom they swept in the Eastern Conference finals, and who bring back a core of four All-Stars — Donovan Mitchell, James Harden, Evan Mobley and Jarrett Allen — while adding a plug-and-play big wing in Peyton Watson. They'll renew unpleasantries with the Indiana Pacers, the last team to beat the Knicks in a playoff series, who are eager to get back up to speed now that Tyrese Haliburton is back and in full form. They'll face off with the Toronto Raptors, who added All-NBA game-breaker Kawhi Leonard to their playoff core. They'll welcome the Miami Heat, who dealt for former MVP Giannis Antetokounmpo. The 68-64 result came Saturday, October 17, at San Francisco’s Chase Center. Reese entered the championship series as the league’s 2026 Defensive Player of the Year, receiving 46 votes from 74 panelists. Online critics questioned her late reaction, although their comments cannot establish precisely what she intended. Michele_Morrone/Depositphotos Atlanta Dream missed a late opportunity Atlanta trailed 66–64 with 23.8 seconds remaining after Golden State center Kiah Stokes made 1 of 2 free throws. The Dream called a timeout to organize their next possession. Rhyne Howard struggled to get past her defender and passed to Allisha Gray. Gray missed a long 3-pointer in the closing seconds, and Golden State reserve Kaila Charles collected the rebound. Mojahid_Mottakin/Depositphotos Angel Reese faced criticism from fans Some viewers on X accused Reese of giving up following Gray’s missed attempt. One commenter urged the forward to keep competing through adversity, while another questioned why she did not immediately pursue the loose ball. Another viewer questioned Reese’s body language throughout the second half, beyond the disputed final play. The posts reflected personal impressions of effort, rather than verified knowledge of what the forward intended during the Finals opener. melis82/Depositphotos A late foul sent Gabby Williams to the line Kaila Charles passed to Gabby Williams after collecting Allisha Gray’s missed attempt. Atlanta fouled Williams with 4.1 seconds remaining, sending her to the free-throw line. Williams made both attempts to extend Golden State’s lead to 68–64. Atlanta failed to score on its final possession, and the Valkyries secured the Game 1 victory. lev radin/Shutterstock.com Angel Reese powered Atlanta’s early lead Reese scored 11 points in the opening quarter, converting five of six field goal attempts. Atlanta finished those 10 minutes ahead 22-14, with the forward repeatedly attacking the basket and finding room near the rim. The Dream closed the quarter with 11 unanswered points after Golden State briefly held a three-point lead. Reese played eight opening minutes, and Atlanta outscored the Valkyries by 13 points during her time on court. Keeton Gale/Shutterstock.com Gabby Williams drove a halftime comeback Golden State erased its first-quarter deficit by scoring 28 points in the second period. The Valkyries led 42-39 at halftime after converting 11 of 16 field goal attempts, while Atlanta made only four of 13. Williams supplied 16 points in that quarter after going scoreless in the first, making six of nine attempts from the field. Her late 3-pointer and a layup following a steal capped Golden State’s 10-0 run. lev radin/Shutterstock.com Angel Reese did not score after half

item.title: Angel Reese to follow up stunning Game 2 performance with release of candy-inspired Angel 1s
item.description: Photo by Paras Griffin/Getty Images WNBA star Angel Reese is launching her Reebok Angel 1s on Tuesday, fresh off the back of what was a starring display in Game 2 of the WNBA Finals. The Dream could not really afford a loss on Monday given they were already a game down in the series, with Reese’s display ensuring that did not happen. She managed 30 points, 16 rebounds and three assists as her team came away with a 79-65 win in Game 2. Now, it has been reported that Reese is launching her Angel 1 shoes on October 20. Angel Reese launching Reebok Angel 1s Tweeting Monday evening, Nick DePaula stated: “Angel Reese is launching the ‘Reese’s’ Reebok Angel 1s tomorrow, an official collab with @Reeses, with a theme inspired by the iconic candy. “‘We designed this colourway especially for my fans, for the Reese’s Pieces!’ says @Reese10Angel.” Reese’s collaboration with Reebok, of course, comes during the same month Caitlin Clark launched her own shoes with Nike. The Caitlin 1s were first released on October 1 and it was reported that they were largely sold out within two hours. Clark and Reese have been rivals since college, so there’s likely to be a lot of chatter from fans about the two WNBA stars having competing shoes. item.description: CLEVELAND, OHIO - OCTOBER 18: Jaleel McLaughlin #38 of the Cleveland Browns runs the ball against the Baltimore Ravens during the fourth quarter of the game at Huntington Bank Field on October 18, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) | Getty Images There’s something about the Browns’ offense in the second half that gets clicking. 237 yards of offense on the day doesn’t sound too impressive, but take into consideration that they only had 46 yards of offense in the first half. Ultimately, they actually out-gained the Ravens, thanks to a strong defensive performance. The team playing complete football (i.e. sticking with things to the end) has worked for four close victories, but to take the next step, they have to obviously break out of that trend to the upside. Below, we analyze the snap counts and stats on offense for the Cleveland Browns ’ Week 6 game against the Baltimore Ravens. Quarterback Pos Player Plays % Snaps Stats QB Deshaun Watson 63 100% 16-of-26 (61.5%) for 164 yards. 8 carries, 29 yards (3.6 YPC). It’s tough to say whether things are processing slower for Deshaun Watson , or if players simply weren’t getting open and he doesn’t want to force the turnover because of that. The announcers kept calling out that players weren’t open, and the few replays that they showed were indicating that as well. I think it’s a mixture of both. I don’t see panic from Watson, but at times, he takes off with what looks to be a decent opening to get some positive yardage. That has worked against some teams, but against the Ravens, their defensive front seemed quicker to close the gap and prevent him from escaping. So if that’s the case against a certain defense, Watson has to discover that balance of perhaps hanging in an extra tick and delivering the ball somewhere. item.description: CHESTNUT HILL, MASSACHUSETTS - JANUARY 18: Donald Hand Jr. #13 of the Boston College Eagles reacts following a three-point basket during the first half of the game against the Duke Blue Devils at Conte Forum on January 18, 2025 in Chestnut Hill, Massachusetts. (Photo by Lance King/Getty Images) | Getty Images Ineffective team 3-point shooting is nothing new. But lately, perhaps due to an extended arc and an increased pro emphasis on long-range scoring, group misfires have become more common. Two of the ACC’s three worst collective efforts from beyond the arc, and five of the worst nine in this century, were registered recently. Lousy long-distance mis-dialing surely played a part in the change of coaching regime at Boston College, where Earl Grant’s fifth Eagles squad made only .294 of their threes, second-worst in the ACC during the 21 st century. Launching threes promises an exciting return for players and fans, a chance to alter the scoring balance emphatically or at least to help fuel a rally or extend a lead. The shot’s elongated arc and extra point value invest the briefest additional sense of anticipation as the ball hangs in the air, hinting at a change in momentum. Let several threes land in a row, or in a flurry, and the crowd, especially at home, will respond enthusiastically. The converse is that the more you miss, the more frustrating the spectacle is to watch. Learning where the carom will land, a habit perfected in practice by savvy players like Matt Harpring, a middlingly athletic forward who excelled at Georgia Tech in the late nineties, can make up for many misses. Or, a player can possess an innate sense of where teammates’ caroms will land, as was the case with NC State’s TJ Warren (2014), who downplayed any offensive rebounding aptitude other than instinct. Still, inaccuracy is deflating, not to mention lending itself to open court fast break opportunities for an opponent. Overall BC trailed all other ACC squads last year in field goal percentage (.408) and 3-point accuracy, and while it played fairly good defense its ballhandling was about as bad as its shooting. Add the fact that Grant conjured a single winning record during his half-decade tenure – 20-16 in 2024 – and managed a single NIT bid, and change was inevitable. Now we’ll see what Luke Murray, late of powerhouse UConn, can do with a program that hasn’t been to the NCAAs since 2009, has modest home court support, no natural ACC rival, and operates within a city rife with other college programs vying for players, attention, and NIL support. None of the Eagles’ first six games are scheduled for venues outside Massachusetts, mirroring the old Syracuse approach of sticking near home as long as possible to start a season. item.description: New York Giants running back Tyrone Tracy Jr. scored two touchdowns in Week 6, but the Giants fell 34-27 to the New Orleans Saints on Sunday. Tracy ran six times for 18 yards and a score, while adding two receptions for 27 yards and another touchdown through the air. Hours later, the 26-year-old became a father of two when he and his wife, Zoe Rollon Tracy, welcomed their twins and announced the birth on social media Monday. Giants RB Tyrone Tracy Jr. and wife Zoe announce twins news New York Giants running back Tyrone Tracy Jr. and his wife, Zoe Rollon Tracy, married in 2026 after getting engaged in January. Tracy is in the third year of his four-year, $4.306 million rookie contract with the team. Following his two-touchdown performance on Sunday, Tracy gave a nod to the news by posting a video clip of his “rock the baby” celebration. He also shared a heartwarming carousel of photos featuring himself, his wife, and their newborn babies from the hospital, writing , “Help me welcome our Twins into this world Blessed by the Lord himself! Couple of Two, Into a Family of 4 TYG ” Under the post, Zoe commented, “Blessed with the sweetest family, I love yall so much most surreal experience of my life” View this post on Instagram A post shared by Tyrone Tracy Jr (@iam_ttjxi) The couple announced the pregnancy in June with photos of a paper titled “The Newborn Times,” listing November as the expected arrival month. Tracy shared his excitement on social media, noting that football season was about to get much more interesting with two little surprises on the way, while offering his thanks to God. One fan wrote, “2TDS on sunday 2 babies on monday congrats ” Another added, “Congratulations you two they are both so gorgeous @_zoetracy” A third penned, “They are so adorable! God bless them both ( and you guys) ! Lots of love ” A fourth wrote, “Enough to make a grown man cry dis is jus beautiful ” NFL players flooded social media to congratulate the couple. Former Giants quarterback Russell Wilson wrote, “What a blessing” Cornerback Greg Newsome II posted, “Congrats fam ” Graham Gano replied, “Aye! Congratulations! What a blessing.” Tracy, whom the Giants selected in the fifth round with the 166th overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft out of Purdue, and Zoe have dated since March 2023. She is a registered oncology nurse. They announced their engagement on Jan. 13 and have since married, making the twins their first children. This season, Tracy holds 13 carries for 40 yards and a touchdown, alongside four catches for 52 yards and a score. The Giants (3-2-1) visit the Houston Texans on Sunday. item.title: Kulusevski a 'different man' after emotional Spurs return
item.description: Tottenham midfielder Dejan Kulusevski was out of action for 17 months (Glyn KIRK) Dejan Kulusevski said he felt like a "different man" after a 17-month injury layoff as he made an emotional return for struggling Tottenham. The Swedish midfielder was introduced to deafening noise in the 87th minute of the club's 3-1 victory against Coventry on Monday at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. Kulusevski had multiple setbacks after knee surgery in May 2025. But a second procedure in March finally set the 26-year-old on the road to recovery. "Everything feels great. I have been working harder than you can ever imagine," Kulusevski said after Tottenham's first Premier League win of the season, which lifted them off the foot of the table. "The journey felt impossible. It was the most difficult it could be, but I had a feeling I was going to come back to play football. I just had to believe and that is what I do." He added: "I kept working, 10 hours every day when no one is watching, so when everything was impossible and everyone gave up I never gave up because of this that happened today. "I am so grateful that (fans) miss(ed) me play. It means a lot and I am here to show them a better me. And a better me will be a better Spurs so we will be good." Tottenham had managed only three home league wins during Kulusevski's lengthy absence and narrowly avoided relegation on the final day of the 2025/26 campaign. He missed the club's Europa League triumph in 2025 and Sweden's World Cup campaign, but is now ready to make up for lost time. "It has been an amazing journey even if it is hard sometimes," he said. "Hard is beautiful and I am so grateful that I had to experience it. "Now I am ready to play football. I see myself a little different now. I think I am a different man now. Same guy, same guy that wants to play football, but a little bit smarter." jw/jdg/nf

item.title: ‘Unnecessary’ — Super Bowl Champ Calls Out Aqib Talib Over Explosive Reaction to Ryan Fitzpatrick’s Bo Nix Rant
item.description: The Denver Broncos are struggling to maintain momentum in the 2026 NFL season. The organization’s quarterback, Bo Nix , has been facing scrutiny because of his recent performances, with questions being raised about his decision-making, composure under pressure, and ability to deliver in crucial moments. A heated debate emerged involving former quarterback Ryan Fitzpatrick and former NFL cornerback Aqib Talib as they discussed the quarterback. Talib was seen talking about Fitzpatrick’s comments on Nix’s performance. Broncos quarterback Bo Nix (10) looks on in the second half against the Seattle Seahawks at Empower Field at Mile High. Mandatory Credit: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images Sherman Calls Talib’s Reaction to Fitzpatrick Unnecessary In a recent episode of the “Richard Sherman Podcast” , Super Bowl champion Richard Sherman shared his views on the debate, describing Talib’s explosive response as “unnecessary” and saying: “I’ve seen some other stuff on the internet. I mean, I saw Fitz’s video to Tlaib after Tlaib tried to get on Fitz about what Fitz said about Bo Nix’s performance. I don’t know what you want in that situation. Bo Nix didn’t play well, and he hasn’t played very well this season. He’s thrown for under 200 yards four times this season alone. It’d be different if you were defending a performance where a guy just had an off day. He’s having an off season right now. “I thought what Fitz did was hilarious. I thought… What Lee did was unnecessary. You can talk about Fitz’s career and ups and downs and whether he won games or not, et cetera, et cetera, but he’s had some stretches where he’s played some outstanding football, thrown for 400 multiple times. I mean, I want to say he threw for 1,200 yards in three weeks at one point. I don’t know if you’ll ever find a stretch of Bo Nix playing that kind of football. He should be playing better. He should have more yardage, and he doesn’t. And if you can’t criticize that, then there’s no point of having a job.” Fitzpatrick shared his views on the quarterback’s performance, as fans are expecting a lot from the young quarterback. On the other hand, former Broncos cornerback Talib is known for his strong football opinions. The disagreement has added another layer to the discussion surrounding Nix and the expectations placed on him. The coming weeks will be critical for the organization, and the discussion ultimately returns to Nix and his development as a quarterback. One bad performance can intensify scrutiny, while strong outings can quickly change the narrative. Nix will need to show greater consistency to reassure fans and silence some of his critics as the Broncos continue their campaign. The debate also highlights the pressure that comes with being a starting quarterback in the NFL. Nix entered the league with high expectations, and fans are eager to see him establish himself as a reliable leader for Denver. Things can get dangerous against a team that lives for such situations.” The lesson for Wednesday is straightforward. Bayern cannot afford to concede unnecessary corners and free kicks, particularly when Arsenal’s delivery and movement inside the penalty area have already caused them so many problems. Mistaking possession for control of the match Bayern’s statistical dominance in possession disguised the extent to which Arsenal controlled the dangerous areas of the pitch. Kompany’s team enjoyed their best spell immediately after Karl’s outstanding 32nd-minute equalizer. Kimmich picked out Serge Gnabry with a magnificent diagonal pass, and the former Arsenal winger redirected the ball into Karl’s path with an equally impressive first-time volley. The 17-year-old finished emphatically, becoming the first player to breach Arsenal’s defense in that season’s Champions League campaign. As Get German Football News’ original player ratings and match analysis highlighted, however, Bayern struggled to reproduce the quality of that attacking move. The visitors became increasingly ineffective after halftime. Arsenal exploited a Kimmich mistake to create an opportunity for Saka in the 48th minute. Merino twice threatened with headers, while Neuer was forced into impressive interventions against Cristhian Mosquera and another dangerous Arsenal attack shortly after the hour mark. Declan Rice, who earned Kicker’s Man of the Match honors, repeatedly helped Arsenal impose themselves in midfield. Bayern’s established attacking stars offered relatively little in response. Michael Olise found himself largely neutralized by Myles Lewis-Skelly, while Harry Kane struggled to make an impact inside the penalty area despite regularly dropping deeper to participate in buildup play. Olise will not have an opportunity to make amends for that performance on Wednesday. The French international is suspended for the rematch , leaving Kompany without one of his most important attacking players. Kane’s difficulties were especially significant given the English striker’s increasingly sophisticated role under Kompany. Against Arsenal, those creative qualities were largely prevented from producing meaningful opportunities. Bayern will need more than a statistical advantage in possession on Wednesday. Finding ways to penetrate Arsenal’s midfield and provide Kane with effective support in advanced areas will be considerably more important. Making costly mistakes against Arsenal’s aggressive pressing Bayern’s problems in possession were not confined to a lack of attacking penetration. The visitors repeatedly endangered themselves with misplaced passes and questionable decisions when attempting to play through Arsenal’s pressure. Kimmich’s error shortly after halftime was one example, although Bayern escaped punishment on that occasion. Dayot Upamecano’s mistake in the 69th minute proved considerably more consequential. The French international surrendered possession while attempting to build from the back, allowing Arsenal to construct another dangerous attacking move. Riccardo Calafiori, who had only just entered the match, eventually found space on the left and delivered a cross toward the far post. Noni Madueke arrived to finish from close range, restoring Arsenal’s lead. Upamecano had already endured a difficult evening. The defender received an early booking for a challenge on Mosquera and was fortunate to escape a second yellow card following another foul on Madueke shortly before the hour mark. The Frenchman also struggled with Eberechi Eze’s movement, frequently following the attacking midfielder into different areas of the pitch. For Wednesday’s rematch, maintaining composure during buildup will be particularly important. Leaving the defense exposed during transitions Bayern’s final major mistake provided the most memorable image of the entire encounter. With the visitors pushing forward in search of another equalizer, Arsenal launched a counterattack in the 77th minute. The Brazilian simply carried the ball beyond the Bayern captain before advancing toward an empty net and converting Arsenal’s third. Neuer’s decision attracted considerable criticism afterward. The pass was good and he scored.” Kompany subsequently defended the principle behind Neuer’s decision, questioning whether the keeper should have remained passive while an opposing attacker advanced toward his goal. Deion Sanders doubled, Terry Pendleton singled, and David Justice drove in Sanders with another single. Fortunately, Guzman managed to limit the damage. The Braves intentionally walked Carter, and Dave Winfield executed one of his rare sacrifice bunts (just 19 in 22 seasons). item.title: Dan Quinn denies video evidence he didn’t know it was fourth down
item.description: Credit: ESPN The Washington Commanders lost again to the San Francisco 49ers and once again drew embarrassing game-management accusations against head coach Dan Quinn and quarterback Jayden Daniels. A week after Daniels, Quinn, and the Commanders inexplicably ran out the clock in overtime against the Giants while in field goal range to win, another strange play occurred on Monday Night Football against the favored 49ers in San Francisco. Down 13-3 in the second quarter and facing 4th & 2 from the 12-yard line, the Commanders quarterback again made a bizarre decision by throwing the ball away and turning the ball over on downs. 200 IQ play. Jayden Daniels throws the ball OUT OF BOUNDS on 4th down to avoid accidentally throwing a touchdown. https://t.co/Pxj4Bn0rTf — Hater Report (@HaterReport) October 20, 2026 Even more peculiar, ESPN’s sideline camera caught Dan Quinn clearly mouthing for the field goal unit to come on the field and then becoming frustrated when he realized it was fourth down. It doesn’t take an expert lip reader to see that’s clearly what happened. this is SOOOO BAD how does the HEAD COACH not know the down??? https://t.co/UaXmbWzgvj — Warren Sharp (@SharpFootball) October 20, 2026 However, after the game, Dan Quinn tried to say that the millions of eyes that saw him call for the field goal unit were lying to them and that he knew it was fourth down all along. “I definitely knew it was 4th down.” Commanders HC Dan Quinn on the 4th down play that Jayden Daniels threw the ball away in the second quarter. https://t.co/SiBP2SIClg — ESPN (@espn) October 20, 2026 “I definitely knew it was fourth down. We were going for it and I was probably saying like with the illegal shift there’s not a penalty to go for a field goal. It’s the turn on downs; I think somebody had asked me,” Quinn said, attempting to explain the video. Sooo… he shouted field goal even though he knew that a penalty on the Commanders and the throwaway would result in a turnover on downs? A better explanation is that he was kicking himself for not taking the points and kicking the field goal. At least that would make more logical sense. Instead, we’re left to believe Daniels, not Quinn, didn’t know what down it was. It’ll be another fun week of finger-pointing in DC over who is most at fault for the team’s failing fortunes. The only thing that everyone can agree on is that Quinn, Daniels, and the Commanders look like a shadow of the team that was in the NFC Championship Game just two seasons ago. A week after Daniels, Quinn, and the Commanders inexplicably ran out the clock in overtime against the Giants while in field goal range to win, another strange play occurred on Monday Night Football against the favored 49ers in San Francisco. Down 13-3 in the second quarter and facing 4th & 2 from the 12-yard line, the Commanders quarterback again made a bizarre decision by throwing the ball away and turning the ball over on downs. 200 IQ play. Jayden Daniels throws the ball OUT OF BOUNDS on 4th down to avoid accidentally throwing a touchdown. https://t.co/Pxj4Bn0rTf — Hater Report (@HaterReport) October 20, 2026 Even more peculiar, ESPN’s sideline camera caught Dan Quinn clearly mouthing for the field goal unit to come on the field and then becoming frustrated when he realized it was fourth down. It doesn’t take an expert lip reader to see that’s clearly what happened. this is SOOOO BAD how does the HEAD COACH not know the down??? https://t.co/UaXmbWzgvj — Warren Sharp (@SharpFootball) October 20, 2026 However, after the game, Dan Quinn tried to say that the millions of eyes that saw him call for the field goal unit were lying to them and that he knew it was fourth down all along. “I definitely knew it was 4th down.” Commanders HC Dan Quinn on the 4th down play that Jayden Daniels threw the ball away in the second quarter. https://t.co/SiBP2SIClg — ESPN (@espn) October 20, 2026 “I definitely knew it was fourth down. We were going for it and I was probably saying like with the illegal shift there’s not a penalty to go for a field goal. It’s the turn on downs; I think somebody had asked me,” Quinn said, attempting to explain the video. Sooo… he shouted field goal even though he knew that a penalty on the Commanders and the throwaway would result in a turnover on downs? A better explanation is that he was kicking himself for not taking the points and kicking the field goal. At least that would make more logical sense. Instead, we’re left to believe Daniels, not Quinn, didn’t know what down it was. It’ll be another fun week of finger-pointing in DC over who is most at fault for the team’s failing fortunes. The only thing that everyone can agree on is that Quinn, Daniels, and the Commanders look like a shadow of the team that was in the NFC Championship Game just two seasons ago. Nothing erudite, anyway. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! It is quite funny that PSG felt like the good guys at the Etihad Stadium but if we briefly detach ourselves from the notion that the European champions’ own sportswashing and cashsplashing has also done immeasurable damage to the beautiful game, then their 4-2 Bigger Cup shellacking of Manchester City was pure cinema, baby! I was stunned at reading the comments in support of Manchester City keeping their trophies, coming out of the mouth of their Bigger Cup rivals at PSG (yesterday’s Quote of the Day). Given the example of the organisers of the Tour de Lance … sorry, the Tour de France, this kind of ‘keep the awards you won’ stuff might get him sent to the Bastille. Or consider Formula One. They’ve got all kinds of rules about driver behaviour on the racetrack, and additional rules about what the crew can and cannot do to your car. Cars get inspected before each race, and there are also mandatory post-race inspections for every car. You might drive your car first across the line to the cheers of the crowd, but if the post-race inspection discovered that you cheated in how your team designed your vehicle, your memory of crossing the line is all you get to keep. Think about that for a minute. If the Premier League and Fifa cannot clear the bar for morals in sport set by the UCI and FIA, that says a lot. And none of it good” – Peter Rehwaldt. My friend Bernard grew up in Coventry. And as a boy he thought the team was called ‘Coventry City Nil’. I would get out more, but I’m a Manchester United fan” – Brendan Hughes. Minor deviations from the familiar, almost imperceptible to outsiders, can set off alarm bells: what’s really going on there? Why isn’t he happy? What’s she hinting at? But it’s an argot developed to talk about football, and when applied to other subjects, it can sound extremely jarring. Erling Haaland is one of the brighter, more engaging players. item.title: Why we’re stuck with a Premier League in the clutches of the global mega-rich | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s little prospect of the model changing in a country that welcomes wealthy international owners with open arms Football, the world’s most popular sport, played by laws drawn up in London in 1863. The Premier League is the UK’s greatest soft power export. Premier League clubs are owned by a deputy prime minister of Abu Dhabi, the public investment fund of Saudi Arabia, a billionaire based in Monaco for tax reasons and a disappointing assortment of investors and private equity funds. And what, really, could be more British than that? Football truly is the national game. What the Manchester City case has exposed is just how difficult it is to regulate some of the richest and most powerful bodies in the world. While the wait for the verdict was frustrating, it was perhaps unavoidable given the possibility of legal objection at every turn when a leaked email from City’s in-house lawyer during Uefa’s action against the club had threatened to “ spend 30 million on the 50 best lawyers in the world to sue them for the next 10 years”. You didn’t get that with Albert Alexander Sr or Peter Swales. Continue reading...

item.title: The Premier League so far: draws, underperforming xG and other data pointers
item.description: Goal averages are crumbling as players take fewer touches in the box and forwards underperform against xG Goals are on the up in the Premier League. The average of 2.70 non-penalty goals per game in 2026-27 is higher than last season and two of the four previous campaigns. Yet we should have been even more royally entertained. Matches have averaged 2.88 non-penalty expected goals, the second most in the past six seasons. Chances have been going to waste. If the 20 teams converted at the par rate, there would have been almost two extra goals per week. As few as that sounds, the proportion of games drawn is higher than in any past Premier League season. Some tied matches might have been settled had the finishing been up to the mark. item.description: From transfers to stadium works and even the training-ground dog, there is no doubting the Spaniard’s influence at the club If anyone doubts Mikel Arteta’s status as No 1 at Arsenal in the week he committed his future to the club until 2030 , just ask Win the dog. Kai Havertz, David Raya and Mikel Merino, who issues commands in Spanish and has spoken about spending time with Win when out for three months with a foot injury, are particular favourites. item.title: Lionel Messi’s Argentina career turned football into a sacred mystery
item.description: Jorge Messi wanted his country to fall in love with his son. That ambition was fulfilled during a brilliant international career that ended this week “What Argentina is doing in this World Cup is of a sacred order,” Brazilian writer Milly Lacombe posted at the height of the tide of anti-Argentinian sentiment during this year’s tournament. She was exploring the contradiction she felt around her support of Lionel Messi: “a player who is a God and a man who shakes Trump’s hand”. Lacombe highlighted the importance of acknowledging the complexities around Messi and the Argentinian team. How is it possible that Messi was not speaking out against the racist incidents we all saw around the Argentina team , she asked. “That’s why it hurts so much to see someone with Messi’s power choosing to make himself small,” she wrote. item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
